guidance: Do not pad with generic phrases such as intense, high detail, beautiful scene, perfect anatomy, dynamic composition, realistic or soft lighting unless the user actually requested that dimension.
Every explicit visual fact from the user is a hard requirement. Prefer deterministic preservation over creative substitution.
If hair, eyes, body type, identity or outfit are unspecified, leave them unspecified instead of inventing them.
Do not infer an unspecified partner gender from an interaction. Subject count/type and partner identity are separate dimensions.
Camera angle, framing and subject gaze/head direction are separate controls. Never normalize one into another.
Posture and camera are separate dimensions; they may coexist without being synonyms.
Mouth state and emotion are separate. Compatible controls such as smile + parted lips may coexist.
Use one dominant camera/view instruction unless the user explicitly requests a compound framing. Do not invent wide angle, fisheye or dynamic angle as decoration.
When a required limb relation has no reliable compact tag, keep one short precise prose atom rather than inventing a pseudo-tag.
Background blur, depth of field and bokeh are related but not synonyms. Use only the controls that match the requested visual effect.
Keep verified lighting/effect controls distinct from community prose. Do not replace rim lighting with backlighting or soft lighting with soft focus automatically.
When NovelAI Add Quality Tags is enabled, avoid duplicating the automatic quality preamble unless deliberately testing it.
Community prompts are retrieval examples and hypotheses, not canonical tag proof. Preserve evidence labels.
For uncertain community recipes, change one variable at a time, keep settings/seed comparable where practical, repeat across multiple generations and record failures as well as successes.

For explicit interaction prompts, keep action anchors separate from posture/orientation, limb placement, camera, render effects and environment. Do not translate the whole interaction into one English sentence.
